steps.title: Label tubes and prepare beads
steps.instruction: Pre‑label all tube strips using a unique project‑name scheme and verify with the PI; then pre‑load cleaned, autoclaved beads into each strip (use a bead dispenser if available).

steps.title: Add leaf tissue to tubes
steps.instruction: Add 10 mg (up to a maximum of 30 mg) of dried leaf material to each bead‑containing tube, rolling/folding the tissue to fit the tube mouth; keep tubes capped when not being loaded and clean tube sides after each addition.

steps.title: Grind tissue in bead tubes
steps.instruction: Place the strips in a tissue lyser and grind for 2 min at a frequency of 30 Hz (1 s⁻¹); repeat grinding if material is not finely powdered.

steps.title: Prepare CTAB extraction buffer
steps.instruction: In the hood, dispense 600 µL of CTAB extraction buffer per sample (+8–10 % excess) into a wide trough, add 1 µL β‑mercaptoethanol per 600 µL buffer, stir, then add 4 µL RNase A per sample; keep β‑mercaptoethanol in a dedicated L200 bottle inside the hood.

steps.title: Add CTAB buffer to samples
steps.instruction: Carefully uncap the ground‑sample tubes, discard caps into waste, and add 600 µL of the prepared CTAB buffer to each tube with a multichannel pipettor; recap tightly with fresh caps.

steps.title: Homogenize samples in buffer
steps.instruction: Vortex or run the tissue lyser briefly to fully homogenize each sample; ensure no powder remains at the tube bottom.

steps.title: Incubate samples at 60 °C
steps.instruction: Incubate the capped strips in a 60 °C water bath for ~20 min (place a brick and paper towel on top to keep caps from popping off); invert the plates at least once, then retighten caps.

steps.title: Pellet debris by centrifugation
steps.instruction: Remove the plates from the water bath, blot dry, retighten caps, and centrifuge for 2 min at 4000 rpm to pellet solids.

steps.title: Transfer supernatant to new plate
steps.instruction: Using a multichannel pipettor with filtered tips, transfer as much supernatant as possible to a newly labelled 96‑well Costar plate; if tips clog, gently bounce them on the beads. Reserve the bead‑containing strips for later recovery.

steps.title: Add chloroform and mix
steps.instruction: Decant chloroform into a hard‑plastic trough, rinse fresh tips 1–2 times with chloroform, then add 500 µL chloroform (equal volume to supernatant) to each tube; recap tightly with fresh caps and avoid drips.

steps.title: Invert samples for chloroform extraction
steps.instruction: Hand‑invert each tube for 5 min using a paper towel over the lids to catch any leakage.

steps.title: Separate phases by centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the plates for 15 min at 4000 rpm to separate the aqueous (upper) and chloroform (lower) layers.

steps.title: Collect aqueous phase into fresh tubes
steps.instruction: While the centrifuge is running, label a fresh strip‑tube plate for final samples and set up a cut‑down rack that shows the phase interface; using filtered tips, pipet up to 300 µL of the clear aqueous layer from each source strip into the matching empty strip, moving chloroform waste to a separate waste plate; avoid drawing interface debris or chloroform.

steps.title: Precipitate DNA with isopropanol
steps.instruction: Add 1.5 volumes of cold 100 % isopropanol to each aqueous sample (e.g., 200 µL sample + 300 µL isopropanol), cap with fresh strip caps, and mix by inverting the plate 1–2 times.

steps.title: Incubate precipitation at –20 °C
steps.instruction: Place the plate in a –20 °C freezer for at least 30 min (or overnight) to allow DNA to precipitate.

steps.title: Pellet DNA by centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the plate for 15 min at 4000 rpm; a grey‑gelatinous pellet should be visible at the tube bottom.

steps.title: Remove isopropanol supernatant
steps.instruction: Uncap the tubes (caps can be reused if laid in order on a labelled towel), tilt each strip to pour off the isopropanol into a dedicated waste tip‑box lid, then blot the open ends with a fresh towel to remove residual liquid.

steps.title: Wash pellet with 70 % ethanol
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL cold molecular‑grade 70 % ethanol to each tube, flick to rinse the pellet (it should float), then centrifuge at 4500 rpm for 5 min; pour off ethanol and wick out remaining liquid with paper towel.

steps.title: Dry pellet at room temperature
steps.instruction: Air‑dry the pellets for 1–2 h at room temperature with a Kimwipe covering the open tubes; if longer drying is needed, loosely recap and continue drying, but avoid overdrying.

steps.title: Resuspend DNA in TE buffer
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL TE buffer to each dried pellet, recap with retained or new caps, flick to mix, and let stand at room temperature for at least 1 h (or refrigerate if used within weeks). Do not freeze before the pellet is fully resuspended; adjust volume (e.g., 20 µL for low‑yield samples, 100 µL for high‑yield) if needed.

steps.title: Store samples at –80 °C
steps.instruction: Place the TE‑resuspended tubes at –80 °C for at least 1 h before freeze‑drying.

steps.title: Prepare freeze dryer
steps.instruction: Turn on the freeze dryer and attached blue pump; allow ~30 min for the system to reach operating conditions.

steps.title: Load samples into freeze dryer
steps.instruction: When the display reads “Load/Unload”, load the –80 °C‑stored tubes into the dryer (do not stack; stagger to minimize contact).

steps.title: Run freeze‑drying cycle
steps.instruction: Start the dryer and run for 48 h; do not stack samples during the run.

steps.title: Aerate dryer and unload samples
steps.instruction: After 48 h, click “Aerate” to stop the machine, remove the red cap on the left side to release collected moisture, and unload the dried tubes.

steps.title: Final centrifugation to settle powder
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the dried tubes for 2 min at 2000 rpm to collect any powder that may have adhered to caps back to the tube bottom before opening.
